findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders a hard-coded empty table
findings.body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the widget table is rendered as `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`. The actual query result (`result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, `fieldAliases`, title, loading state, custom field renderers) is never passed through, and because `columns` is `[]` (not nullish) the component's fallback to derive columns from `tableData.meta.fields` is also bypassed. Any organization that gets this flag will see completely blank table widgets instead of their data. Either wire the real `result`/`fields` into the new component or keep the branch out of the released code path.

findings.title: fetch_error_details pairs error IDs with nodestore values by dict order
findings.body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns its results in the same order as the input list and includes an entry for every requested node id. That is only true for the naive dict-comprehension backend; other backends (e.g. Bigtable, which returns rows in row-key order, and caches that skip misses) can return a differently ordered and/or shorter mapping. The result is `ErrorEvent.id` values attached to the wrong event payload, and silently dropped/mismatched errors. Iterate over `node_ids`/`error_ids` and look the data up by node id instead (`events.get(node_id)`).

findings.title: Error/breadcrumb interleaving compares seconds against milliseconds
findings.body: `gen_request_data` orders errors relative to replay events with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. The error timestamp comes from nodestore event data, which is a Unix timestamp in seconds (~1.7e9), while rrweb recording events carry `timestamp` as epoch milliseconds (~1.7e12). Every error will therefore compare as "earlier" than every breadcrumb and all error log lines will be emitted before any breadcrumb, destroying the chronological context the feature is built to provide. The new tests don't catch this because the fixtures build segment events with second-resolution timestamps; please normalize units (and add a test with realistic millisecond rrweb timestamps).

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter is skipped unless a search query is typed
findings.body: `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` early when `searchQuery` is empty, and only applies the `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` filter in the search branch. As a result `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are shown in the attributes tree by default and disappear only while the user is searching — the opposite of the intent, and visibly inconsistent behavior. The hidden-attribute filter should be applied to the base list before the search short-circuit.

findings.title: get_environment_info issues a Snuba + DB query per issue inside comment generation
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` (a Snuba event lookup) followed by `event.get_environment()` (a DB/environment lookup) for every issue, and both GitHub and GitLab `get_comment_body` call it once per issue in a list comprehension. That adds up to 5 extra Snuba queries plus environment fetches per PR/MR comment, on a path that previously only used already-loaded `Group` fields. Consider resolving the environment in bulk (or from data already available on the group) instead of per-issue, and note that the broad `except Exception` silently degrades to no environment, so these failures would be hard to notice.

findings.title: One nonconforming report causes the entire batch to be dropped with 422
findings.body: The loop validates each report and returns `422` for the whole request as soon as any single report fails, so all other (valid) reports in the same POST are discarded and never counted. This is risky for a data-collection endpoint: the serializer requires `destination` and `attempts` (fields the Reporting API spec does not include in the delivered payload — browsers send `age`/`type`/`url`/`user_agent`/`body`) and restricts `type` to a fixed `BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES` choice list, so newly introduced or spec-variant report types will now fail hard instead of being measured. Prefer validating per report and skipping/counting invalid ones (with a metric/log) while still returning 200 for the rest.

findings.title: Custom cell renderers returning falsy nodes are silently replaced by the default renderer
findings.body: `TableWidgetVisualization`'s prop docs (and the story) state that returning `undefined` from `renderTableBodyCell`/`renderTableHeadCell` falls back to the default renderer, but the implementation checks `if (cell)`. A custom renderer that legitimately returns `null`, `''`, `0` or `false` (e.g. to render an intentionally blank cell) will be overridden by the default field renderer. Check explicitly for `undefined` (`if (cell !== undefined)`).

findings.title: Header alignment is derived from the display name instead of the column key
findings.body: `fieldAlignment(column.name, column.type as ColumnValueType)` passes the human-readable column label. When a caller supplies custom display names without an explicit `type` (the documented use case — e.g. `{key: 'count(span.duration)', name: 'Count of Span Duration'}` in the spec fixture), `fieldAlignment` falls back to name-based detection and cannot recognize the aggregate/numeric field, so numeric columns are left-aligned. Use `column.key` for the field argument.

findings.title: Assemble analytics recorded before the feature check and payload validation
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs at the top of `post`, before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature gate and before schema validation. Every probe/404 and every malformed request is therefore counted as an assemble call, which makes the metric unusable for measuring real usage. Move the record after the feature check (and ideally after validation succeeds).

findings.title: 60s processing deadline may be too short for a 100-identity chunk, silently skipping identities
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` processes up to `chunk_size=100` identities serially, each performing an external IdP `refresh_identity` network call, under the new `processing_deadline_duration=60`. That is a ~0.6s budget per identity. If the deadline is hit the task is killed, but `check_auth` has already bumped `last_synced` for the whole batch, so the unprocessed identities will not be re-selected until the next ~24h cutoff and their SSO validity silently goes unchecked. Either raise the deadline, lower the default chunk size, or only update `last_synced` after an identity is actually processed.

findings.title: No-op migration comments point to a migration that isn't in this change
findings.body: Both 0917 and 0920 are gutted to `return` with the comment "See 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py for the correct migration." No such migration is added in this PR, so unless 0921 already exists on the base branch the comment is a dangling reference and a future reader cannot find the replacement migration. Please land the referenced migration together with these no-ops or fix the pointer.

findings.title: `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` guard is always true
findings.body: `normalizeDateTimeParams(selection.datetime)` always returns an object, so `Boolean(normalizedDateRange)` is unconditionally `true` and the `enabled` option is effectively just the feature-flag check. If the intent was to avoid firing the request before page filters are ready, the guard needs to inspect an actual field (e.g. `statsPeriod`/`start`/`end`) or use `usePageFilters().isReady`; otherwise drop the dead condition.

findings.title: Merged-PR comment template's trailing newline produces blank lines between issues
findings.body:
`MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` now ends with `
`, while both GitHub and GitLab build the list with `"
".join(...)`. The rendered comment therefore has a blank line between every issue and an extra blank line before the trailing `<sub>Did you find this useful?...</sub>` footer (visible in the updated test expectations as `


<sub>`). Drop the trailing newline from the template (or join with `""`) so the bullet list renders as a compact list.

findings.title: Error context silently empty for replays older than the default stats period
findings.body: `self.get_filter_params(request, project)` falls back to the default stats period (14 days) when the caller doesn't pass `statsPeriod`/`start`/`end`, and those bounds are used for the `query_replay_instance` lookup that produces `error_ids`. For a replay older than the default window the Snuba query returns nothing, `error_ids` is empty, and the summary is generated without any error context with no indication to the caller. Derive the time range from the replay itself (or require explicit bounds and return an error when the replay isn't found).
